text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The cement company Cimpor will invest 80 billion escudos in Spain, Brasil, Tunisia and Morrocco up to 2000 in the privatisation of companies there.
- European Commission forecasts for the year 2000 do not favor Portugal because Northern countries are not seen approving increases in structural funding.
- More than 54 percent of Portuguese would like a reshuffle of ruling Socialist government.
- Oil company Petrogal will reinforce its international strategy by selling its engine oils through Autosil in the French market.
- The Ford/Volkswagen company, Autoeuropa, will be the first factory in Portugal to use natural gas in its production process, reducing its energy costs.

- The association between paper pulp company Portucel and Spanish company Ence, as well as its partnership with Brasilian construction company Odebrecht are on hold due to government decision to restructure sector.
- The Finance Ministry has forecast a small surplus in social security accounts for the year 2000, appearing to contradict the Social Security Ministry's own accounts.
